children: Jefferies expects the S&P 500 to climb to 9,000 by the end of 2027, but the bullish forecast is not built on investors paying ever-higher valuations. Instead, the bank is betting that corporate earnings can rise sharply enough to carry the market higher, with profit growth broadening beyond mega-cap technology companies even as inflation, bond yields and AI-related risks remain elevated.
For 2026, Jefferies sees the S&P 500 ending at 8,000, supported by earnings per share of $373 and a 21.5-times price-to-earnings multiple.

Jefferies expects S&P 500 earnings to rise to $450 per share, which would support a 9,000 target even if the valuation multiple falls to 20 times earnings. That distinction matters because the forecast depends primarily on companies delivering stronger profits rather than another round of multiple expansion.

The bank expects earnings growth of 35% in 2026, above the broader consensus estimate of 29%. Consensus expectations have already strengthened substantially, rising from roughly 13% growth at the start of the year.
Artificial intelligence remains central to the thesis. Jefferies estimates companies with direct or indirect exposure to AI and data-center spending now represent about 46% of the S&P 500.

But the firm also expects the earnings recovery to widen. Magnificent Seven companies are projected to deliver roughly 45% earnings growth in 2026, while the rest of the index could still post around 24% growth. That would make the rally less dependent on a handful of technology giants.

Jefferies' 9,000 target ultimately rests on earnings delivery, not valuation expansion. Investors should watch whether 2027 EPS estimates continue moving toward $450, whether profit growth broadens beyond mega-cap tech, and whether AI spending translates into sustained corporate earnings. Inflation, rising Treasury yields and higher oil prices could pressure the market's valuation multiple, while any slowdown in AI-linked earnings would challenge the forecast. The bullish case becomes considerably stronger if earnings estimates keep rising even as the S&P 500's multiple stays near or below current levels.

title: Jefferies Sets Jaw-Dropping S&P 500 Target for 2027
